How to do itDumbbell Lateral Raise

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Handle mid-palm, thumb wrapped, wrist straight.

Wrong: In the fingers, thumb loose, hand pulled down.

Hold the handle mid-palm, so your wrist stays straight. At the top, keep your little finger no higher than your thumb.

Top height: right and wrong

Right
SHOULDER HEIGHT
Wrong
TOO HIGH

Right: Shoulder height, elbow no lower than the hand.

Wrong: Arm raised well above shoulder height.

Shoulders: right and wrong

Right
NECK LONG
Wrong
SHRUG

Right: Shoulders down, away from your ears.

Wrong: Shoulders hunched up toward the ears.

The upper traps stay quiet. No shrug.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. ShrugThe shoulders shrug toward the ears.
  2. DipThe knees dip to swing it up.
  3. Thumbs downThumbs turn down at the top.
Lift1 s
Hold0.5 s
Lower2 s
Rest0.5 s
Look closer

Grip

Hold the handle mid-palm, so your wrist stays straight. At the top, keep your little finger no higher than your thumb.

Wrist bending past about 15 degrees? Too heavy, or you're lifting with your hands.

Common handling mistakes

  • Little finger up

    Fix: At the top, palms down, thumbs level with little fingers.

  • Swinging and shrugging

    Fix: Go lighter, body still, shoulders down.

  • Too high

    Fix: Stop at shoulder height, then lower with control.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this on the outside of your shoulders. If your neck takes over, go lighter.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou're shrugging, lifting too heavy, or raising above shoulder height.

    FixGo lighter, shoulders down, stop at shoulder height. Some trap work is normal.

  • Usually meansLittle finger tipping up, or arms going too high.

    FixKeep thumbs level and stop at shoulder height. If it still pinches, stop the exercise.

  • Usually meansSqueezing too hard, handle in your fingers, or a bent wrist.

    FixMove the handle to mid-palm, thumb wrapped. Hold firm but relaxed.

  • Usually meansYou're leaning back to swing the weight up.

    FixGo lighter, body still. Or sit on a bench.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Pick dumbbells you can raise 12 to 20 times without swinging.

  2. 2

    Feet hip width, knees soft. Swinging? Sit on a bench.

  3. 3

    Dumbbells by your thighs, palms in, grip mid-palm.

  4. 4

    Keep your elbows soft, arms a little in front.

  5. 5

    Shoulders down and slightly back, neck long.

Risks and when to stop

  • Above shoulder height or little finger up can pinch a shoulder tendon.
  • Shrugging and swinging shift the work to your neck and lower back.
  • A handle in your fingers bends your wrist and adds forearm and shoulder work.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

How to do itBarbell Back Squat

Hand: right and wrong

Option: thumb over the bar

If a wrapped thumb bends your wrist back.

Bar low in your palm, wrist straight.

In your fingers, hand bent back like a tray.

Your back holds the bar. Your hands just pin it, in the heel of your palm.

Bar on back: right and wrong

On your upper traps, below the bony bump.

On the bony bump at your neck.

Depth: right and wrong

Hip crease at or below the top of your knee.

Hip stops well above your knee.

The bar travels straight down and up over the middle of the foot.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips rise firstThe hips come up before the shoulders.
  2. Chest dropsThe chest falls and the trunk tips forward.
  3. Bar drifts forwardThe bar moves out over the toes.
Lower2 s
Drive up1 s
Brace1 s
Look closer

Grip

Your back holds the bar. Your hands just pin it, in the heel of your palm.

Wrist folding back or taking weight? Your hands are holding the bar up.

Common handling mistakes

  • Hands holding the bar up

    Fix: Elbows down, so your back holds the bar.

  • Knees caving or heels lifting

    Fix: Knees out over toes, heels down. Still caving? Go lighter.

  • Hips shoot up, back rounds

    Fix: Brace. Chest and hips rise together.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs and glutes. If your lower back does more, go lighter.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

Your trunk works like a tight belt.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour hands are holding the bar up, not your back.

    FixPull your elbows down. Move your hands until your wrists sit straight.

  • Usually meansHips rising first, a soft brace, or rounding at the bottom.

    FixBrace, lift chest and hips together, and stop before your back rounds.

  • Usually meansKnees caving in, heels lifting, or bouncing at the bottom.

    FixPush your knees out over your toes, heels down, and lower with control.

  • Usually meansA wrapped thumb can bend your wrist back, adding pain.

    FixTry your thumb over the bar. Keep whichever holds your wrist straighter.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Collars on, pins just below your lowest squat to catch a miss.

  2. 2

    Squeeze your shoulder blades so the bar rests on muscle.

  3. 3

    Breathe into your belly, brace, and stand the bar up.

  4. 4

    Step back, feet hip to shoulder width, toes out a little.

  5. 5

    Stuck? Lower the bar onto the pins. Don't throw it.

Risks and when to stop

  • Hips shooting up or a rounding back loads your lower back far more.
  • High blood pressure? Don't hold your breath long. Breathe out as you stand.

Severe pain, badly swollen, changed shape, locking, giving way, or can't put weight on it? Get it checked today.

How to do itPull-up

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Bar where fingers start, thumb wrapped.

Wrong: Bar at the fingertips, fingers opening.

Hook the bar where your fingers start, like carrying a bag. Wrap your thumb: you hang from the bar.

Right: Bar where fingers start, thumb wrapped.

Wrong: Bar deep in the palm, skin pinched.

Hook the bar where your fingers start, like carrying a bag. Wrap your thumb: you hang from the bar.

Thumb options, seen from the side

Hook the bar where your fingers start, like carrying a bag. Wrap your thumb: you hang from the bar.

Shoulders: right and wrong

Seen from behind
Right
BLADES DOWN
Wrong
BLADES HIGH

Right: Shoulders down, clear gap to the ears.

Wrong: Shoulders shrugged to the ears.

Top position: right and wrong

Right
HEAD LEVEL
Wrong
CHIN REACHING

Right: Chin over the bar, head level.

Wrong: Chin craning forward, shoulders rolled.

From straight arms, pull until the chin clears the bar, chest toward it.

Look closer

Grip

Hook the bar where your fingers start, like carrying a bag. Wrap your thumb: you hang from the bar.

Bar sliding to your fingertips? End the set.

Common handling mistakes

  • Bouncing at the bottom

    Fix: Lower slowly to straight arms.

  • Grip too wide

    Fix: Hands just outside your shoulders.

  • Bar slipping to fingertips

    Fix: Set the bar where your fingers start.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the sides of your back. Drive your elbows to your ribs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou're shrugging toward your ears.

    FixSet your shoulders down before your arms bend.

  • Usually meansGrip too wide, or your chin reaching for the bar.

    FixBring your hands in, head level. If it keeps hurting, stop pull-ups.

  • Usually meansToo many sets, or a grip your elbows dislike.

    FixTry neutral handles or a shoulder-width grip, and fewer sets.

  • Usually meansBar in your fingertips, wrist curled, or an old injury.

    FixKeep your wrist level. If it's sore, use neutral handles and stop if it hurts.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Bar fixed and dry? Chalk sweaty hands.

  2. 2

    Can't do a few clean reps? Use a band or assisted machine.

  3. 3

    Hands just outside your shoulders, palms away.

  4. 4

    Hang still, legs together.

  5. 5

    Arms straight, shoulders down. Then pull.

Risks and when to stop

  • Dropping into the bottom jerks your weight through the shoulder.
  • Wide grips are linked to shoulder pinching.
  • Chin reaching strains your neck. Fingertip grips can slip off.

How to do itHanging Leg Raise

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Base of the fingers, thumb wrapped, wrist level.

Wrong: Bar at the fingertips, wrist curled.

Bar at the base of your fingers, thumb wrapped, so your hand won't peel open.

Thumb options, seen from the side

Bar at the base of your fingers, thumb wrapped, so your hand won't peel open.

Pelvis curl: right and wrong

Right
PELVIS CURLS UP
Wrong
BACK ARCHES

Right: Pelvis curls up, lower back gently rounded.

Wrong: Legs up, pelvis tipped forward, back arched.

Shoulders: right and wrong

Seen from behind
Right
BLADES DOWN
Wrong
BLADES HIGH

Right: Shoulders pulled down, clear gap to the ears.

Wrong: Shoulders at the ears, head sunk.

At the top, curl the pelvis up toward the ribs so the abs finish the lift.

Tells
  1. SwingThe body swings to fling the legs.
  2. Knees onlyKnees bend; thighs stop short.
  3. Back archesThe low back arches, no curl.
Lift1.5 s
Hold0.5 s
Lower2 s
Rest1 s
Look closer

Grip

Bar at the base of your fingers, thumb wrapped, so your hand won't peel open.

A curling wrist means your grip is failing. End the set or use straps.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging your legs up

    Fix: Start each rep still and lower slower than you lift.

  • Lifting only your legs

    Fix: As your thighs pass hip height, curl your hips toward your ribs.

  • Hanging loose, shoulders sunk

    Fix: Set your shoulders a little down before the first rep.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this down your stomach, most as your hips curl up.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYour pelvis isn't curling, so your hip muscles do the lifting.

    FixBend your knees and curl your hips up toward your ribs.

  • Usually meansYou're swinging, or your back arches as your legs move.

    FixStart still and lower slowly, or use a captain's chair. Stop if it hurts.

  • Usually meansYou're hanging loose, so your shoulders have sunk up to your ears.

    FixPull your shoulders a little down from your ears. Hold them there.

  • Usually meansYour wrist curls as grip fails, or an old injury gets stretched.

    FixKeep your wrist level. If it's sore, use ab slings and stop if it hurts.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Weak grip? Use straps. Sore wrist? Ab slings or a captain's chair.

  2. 2

    Step up from a box, and check it's clear of your legs.

  3. 3

    Chalk up. Bar at shoulder width, palms away, thumb wrapped.

  4. 4

    Hang with straight arms, shoulders pulled a little down from your ears.

  5. 5

    Wait until you hang still. New to this? Start with bent knees.

Risks and when to stop

  • Swinging jerks your weight through your hands and shoulders and arches your lower back.
  • Skipping the hip curl pulls on your lower spine, which matters with back pain.
  • Dropping into a loose hang loads your shoulder, which has little room overhead.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itLat Pulldown

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Bar at the finger base, wrist straight.

Wrong: Wrist curled forward, fist squeezed hard.

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Right: Bar at the finger base, wrist straight.

Wrong: Bar at the fingertips: end the set.

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Thumb options, seen from the side

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Knee pad: right and wrong

Right
PAD ON THIGHS
Wrong
PAD TOO HIGH

Right: Pad firm on the thighs, hips down.

Wrong: Pad too high, hips lifting.

Bar path: right and wrong

Right
IN FRONT
Wrong
BEHIND THE NECK

Right: Bar past the chin to the chest.

Wrong: Bar behind the neck, head pushed forward.

Lean back slightly and pull the bar past the face to the top of the chest.

Pull1 s
Hold0.5 s

Look closer

Grip

Hook the bar at the base of your fingers, wrist straight. Pull with your elbows so your back does more.

Wrist curling, or bar slipping to your fingertips? Finish the rep and end the set.

Sore wrist? Use the neutral-grip handles.

Common handling mistakes

  • Pulling behind your neck

    Fix: Pull in front of your face, to your upper chest.

  • Curling wrists, squeezing hard

    Fix: Straighten your wrist. Grip only as hard as needed.

  • Leaning back and swinging

    Fix: Hold a small lean still and go lighter.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the sides of your back, under your armpits. Drive your elbows down.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou're gripping hard with curled wrists.

    FixLoosen your grip and drive your elbows down.

  • Usually meansYou're rocking, or the knee pad is loose.

    FixSnug the pad, hold a small lean, go lighter.

  • Usually meansBar behind your head, or pulling too far.

    FixPull in front and stop when your elbows stop. If it still pinches, stop pulldowns.

  • Usually meansIt's curling forward, bending sideways, or already sore from pressing.

    FixKeep your wrist straight. If it's sore, use neutral handles and stop if it hurts.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Snug the knee pad so you can't lift off.

  2. 2

    Push the pin fully in. Start light.

  3. 3

    Hands about 1.5 times shoulder width, palms away, thumb wrapped.

  4. 4

    Lean back slightly, about 30 degrees at most.

  5. 5

    Shoulders down, away from your ears. Then pull.

Risks and when to stop

  • Behind-the-neck pulling is linked to a looser front shoulder.
  • Rocking uses your lower back and jerks your shoulders.
  • Pulling past where your elbows stop stresses the shoulder joint.

How to do itSeated Cable Row

Hand: right and wrong

Right: Thumb wrapped, wrist straight.

Wrong: Wrist curled, handle at the fingertips.

Pull with your elbows, not your hands. Handle at the base of your fingers, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.

Back line: right and wrong

Right
BACK STRAIGHT
Wrong
BACK ROUNDED

Right: Arms long, lower back in its normal curve.

Wrong: Lower back rounded, head chasing the handle.

Finish: right and wrong

Right
HANDLE TO BELLY
Wrong
ELBOWS HIGH

Right: Handle at upper belly, elbows just past ribs.

Wrong: Handle at chest, elbows high, shoulders up.

Sit tall; no rocking, the torso finishes upright.

Tells
  1. Swinging backThe torso swings back past upright to heave the weight.
  2. Legs pushThe knees straighten to shove the body back.
Pull1 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s
Rest0.5 s
Look closer

Grip

Pull with your elbows, not your hands. Handle at the base of your fingers, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.

Curling wrists mean your grip is taking over. Finish the rep, then end the set.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rocking your torso

    Fix: Pick a weight you can pull with a still torso.

  • Rounding your lower back

    Fix: Arms go long, back stays tall.

  • Shrugging and flaring elbows

    Fix: Shoulders down, elbows tucked to your ribs.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this between your shoulder blades and down the sides of your back. Lead with your elbows.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou're shrugging, or your elbows flare up.

    FixKeep shoulders down, elbows low and close. Pull to your belly.

  • Usually meansYou're rocking to move the weight, or rounding at the front.

    FixGo lighter and sit tall. Only your arms and shoulder blades move.

  • Usually meansYour elbows go too far back and your shoulders roll forward.

    FixStop once elbows pass your sides, chest up. If light weight still pinches, stop rowing.

  • Usually meansWrists curling or bending to the little finger, or sore from pressing.

    FixKeep your wrist straight. If it's sore, go lighter and stop if it hurts.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Clip on the V-handle. Start light.

  2. 2

    Sit facing the stack, feet flat on the plate.

  3. 3

    Bend your knees, not your back, to take the handle. Thumbs wrapped.

  4. 4

    Sit tall, knees soft. Push back until the weight clears the stack.

  5. 5

    Chest up, shoulders down before you pull. It's hardest at the start.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rocking loads your lower back. Repeated rounding under load hurt discs in lab tests.
  • Shrugging loads your neck. Elbows too far back can pinch your shoulder.
  • Curled wrists tire your forearms first and can make wrists sore over time.

How to do itLeg Press (45°)

Back on pad: right and wrong

Tailbone and lower back flat on the pad.

Too deep: your tailbone peels off the pad.

Feet: right and wrong

Whole foot flat, middle of the plate.

Feet low, heel up, pushing through the ball.

Hand: right and wrong

Held like a shopping bag handle, wrist level.

Pushing on your knee folds the wrist far back.

Your hands just keep you in the seat. Hold lightly, never push on your knees.

Keep the hips and low back pressed into the pad the whole time.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips lift offToo deep; the hips and low back peel off the pad.
  2. Knees caveThe knees fall in toward each other.
  3. Heels liftThe heels peel off the plate.
Lower2 s
Pause0.5 s
Press1 s
Rest0.5 s
Look closer

Grip

Your hands just keep you in the seat. Hold lightly, never push on your knees.

Keep your wrist level, not curled forward or bent far back.

Common handling mistakes

  • Going too deep

    Fix: Stop before your tailbone lifts, around 90 degrees for most people.

  • Snapping knees straight

    Fix: Push until almost straight, keep a small bend, then go again.

  • Knees caving, hands on knees

    Fix: Knees over toes. If you need your hands, take a plate off.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs and glutes. If your lower back works, stop higher.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansToo deep, so your tailbone lifts, or the pad is too upright.

    FixStop higher and set the depth catch there. Recline the pad if it adjusts.

  • Usually meansFeet low with heels up, knees caving, or locking at the top.

    FixMove your feet up, heels down, knees over toes. Stop just short of straight.

  • Usually meansSqueezing hard, or pushing on your knees to finish a rep.

    FixHold the handles lightly. If a rep needs your hands, take a plate off.

  • Usually meansWeight on a sore wrist can make it worse.

    FixHold lightly, wrists level, never on your knees. Stop if it hurts.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Depth catch? Set it just below your lowest point.

  2. 2

    Sit right back, lower back flat on the pad.

  3. 3

    On most machines, push the sled up and turn the handles out.

  4. 4

    Lower to about 90 degrees. Breathe out as you push. Dizzy? Stop.

  5. 5

    Turn the handles in and rest the sled before feet come off.

Risks and when to stop

  • Going too deep bends your lower back under the whole sled.
  • A knee snapped straight under load can bend the wrong way. Rare, but reported.
  • Caving knees twist under load. Hands on knees bend your wrists back.

How to do itMachine Chest Press

Hand: right and wrong

Heel of your palm, thumb wrapped, wrist straight.

Handle in your fingers, wrist bent back, thumb loose.

Push through the heel of your palm, so your wrist stays straight. A wrapped thumb stops the handle rolling into your fingers.

Vertical handles: the same rule.

Sore wrist? Use the vertical handles.

Seat height: right and wrong

Handles meet the middle of your chest.

Seat too low: handles up near your shoulders.

Shoulder blades: right and wrong

Shoulder blades on the pad, elbows slightly bent.

Shoulders roll off the pad, elbows locked.

Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of the chest.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Off the padThe shoulders roll forward and the upper back leaves the pad.
  2. Locked elbowsThe elbows snap straight at the end of the press.
Press1 s
Hold0.3 s
Return1.5 s
Rest0.5 s

Also check your wrist:

Look closer

Grip

Push through the heel of your palm, so your wrist stays straight. A wrapped thumb stops the handle rolling into your fingers.

Wrist bending back past about 15 to 20 degrees? Stop and go lighter.

Sore wrist? Use the vertical handles.

Common handling mistakes

  • Wrist bent back

    Fix: Handle on the heel of your palm. Still bending? Go lighter.

  • Seat too low

    Fix: Raise the seat so the handles meet mid-chest.

  • Shoulders roll off, elbows lock

    Fix: Stop before your elbows lock. Rolling forward to finish? Go lighter.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this across the middle and lower chest. If your shoulders take over, check the seat height.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe handles sit too high, or your shoulders roll off the pad.

    FixCheck the seat height first. On most machines, raise it.

  • Usually meansThe handle has slid into your fingers, so your wrist bends back.

    FixPush from the heel of your palm. Go lighter until your wrist stays straight.

  • Usually meansPressing heavy on a sore wrist can make it worse.

    FixUse the vertical handles and go lighter. Stop the set if it hurts.

  • Usually meansYou snap your elbows straight at the end of each push.

    FixStop just before the elbows lock and control the way back.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the seat so the handles meet mid-chest.

  2. 2

    Start the handles at your chest, never behind it.

  3. 3

    Sit right back, hips on the pad, feet flat.

  4. 4

    Handle in the heel of your palm, wrist straight.

  5. 5

    Set your shoulder blades down and back into the pad.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pushing through a bent-back wrist squeezes the back of the wrist.
  • Handles behind your chest, elbows out, stretch the front of your shoulder under load.
  • Snapping your elbows straight under heavy weight loads the joints, not the muscles.
